answers: Reference: He had power of expression, simplicity, a subtle humor. exercises.title: Translation 5 · passage
exercises.instruction: Translate the following passage, using the words and expressions in brackets.
paragraphs: 富兰克林从小就喜欢读书，把手里的钱都拿去买书。他也会有意识地结交（be acquainted with）一些热爱藏书或者读书的朋友。如果有人能与他讨论或者辩论（dispute） 书中提出的问题，他会与这些人保持更亲密、更持久的关系。富兰克林的哥哥曾鼓励他创作诗歌（compose ballads），爸爸曾提醒他写作中应注重文笔优雅（elegance ofexpression）和章法严谨。为了提高写作水平，富兰克林曾有很长一段时间模仿英国著名杂志《旁观者》的语言。他先从中挑选几篇文章，写出每句话隐含的意思（hinted sentiment），然后不看原书，试着用自己能想到的（come to hand）最贴切的字眼进行表达，再把自己的文章与原文进行对比，发现错误，改正并牢记，以备以后使用。
answers: Franklin was fond of reading from childhood and spent all his money on books. He was ready to get acquainted with people who loved collecting books or reading books. If someone could argue or dispute with him over the ideas outlined in a book, he would want to develop a more intimate and longer lasting friendship. Franklin’s brother once encouraged him to compose ballads, and his father reminded him about his lack of elegance of expression or precise logical structure. For a long time, Franklin imitated the language of the famous English magazine The Spectator to improve his writing. He did this by taking some of the articles and writing down the hinted sentiment in each sentence. Then, without looking at the book, he would try to use any suitable words that should come to hand to express the sentiment. Fianlly he compared his version with the original, discovered his faults, corrected them, and remembered them for future use.

exercises.title: Translation 5 · passage
exercises.instruction: Translate the following passage, using the words and expressions in brackets.
paragraphs: 现在数亿人（inhabitant）居住在城市。城市生活有时需要以失换得。因此，人们需要做出权衡（trade-off）。例如，个人自由（individual freedom）和社区利益（community interests）之间的权衡，社会联结（social ties）和匿名性（anonymity）之间的权衡。在人口密集的（densely populated）新加坡，政府严格检查居民用水情况，管控街道交通，监控汽车行驶以及建筑物的温度和阴影，并跟踪登记水电的消耗，以此换来的（bargain）是一流的生活水平、健康和安全。在德国，政府对屋顶瓦片、树木和钓鱼许可证（fishing license）的规定带来的是美丽的建筑、绿色的城市以及数量可观的鱼群。相反，在洛杉矶，个人财产权被视作神圣不可侵犯，结果是人们自由放任（free-for-all）。在新几内亚乡村地区，传统的生活方式虽然带给了人们相伴一生的朋友和社会的支持，令人倍感温暖（heartwarming），然而这种生活方式也不无缺点：社交上令人窒息（suffocating），也限制了个人的潜能。因此，城市生活的一切最终可归结为（come down to）妥协。
answers: Billions of inhabitants in the world now live in cities. In urban life, gain sometimes means a return for loss. As a result, there are often trade-offs for people to balance, for example, the trade-off between individual freedom and community interests and the trade-off between social ties and anonymity. Densely populated Singapore strictly checks water usage, measures street traffic, car movement, building temperatures and shadows, and tracks water and electricity consumption. It is a bargain for first-class living standards, health, and security. In Germany, the rules about roof tiles, trees, and fishing licenses result in beautiful architecture, green cities, and healthy fish population. In contrast, individual property owner’s rights are seen as sacred in Los Angeles, and this often results in a free-for-all. Surrounded by lifelong friends and social support, traditional living arrangements in rural areas of New Guinea may seem heartwarming, yet there are drawbacks—life here can be socially suffocating and it can also limit individuals’ potential. Ultimately, city life all comes down to compromises.

paragraphs: 食物是社区和文化的重要组成部分。如今异国风味（exotic food）备受青睐，融合亚洲各国风味的亚洲主题美食就是典型的例子。然而，如果认为仅仅通过品尝食物就可以理解某种文化，那就有问题（problematic）了。主流文化把边缘社会（marginalized community） 的食物殖民化（colonize）、商业化（commercialize）、贵族化（gentrify），这种现象叫作文化挪用（cultural appropriation）。企业通过对传统食物进行改良（repurpose）获取利润, 结果当地社群遭受压榨（oppression），便宜的食物（cheap eats）不复存在。因此，在享用美食的同时，我们也应该思考（reflect upon）食物、人和权力三者之间的关系。

Cultural appropriation occurs when the dominant culture gets food from marginalized communities and starts to colonize, commercialize and gentrify it. answers: Uyehara’s way of traveling—to travel like a cultural interloper—is no longer popular today.
“Travel Like a Local” is a silly paradoxical myth; at worst, it’s terrible vacation advice. For one thing, locals aren’t traveling. For another, you simply cannot travel like a local.

Being a vulnerable, ignorant tourist sometimes can even get you special treatment such as the hospitality of local people. It makes you wonder whether acting like a tourist in your hometown seems to be a better way to approach everyday life.

exercises.instruction: Translate the following passage, using the words and expressions in brackets.
paragraphs: 过去，密西西比河每一天都在它1,200英里长的河道上向世人毫无遮拦地（without reserve）展现它的奇观。它如此引人入胜（absorbing），如此蓬勃不衰（unflagging），如此光芒闪耀（sparking）。河面的日落如此美妙。而现在，它所有的优雅、美丽和诗意对我而言都不复存在（restore）。如果河水被夕阳照亮，则表示明天会有风。如果出现漂浮的原木（floating log），则说明河水正在上涨。如果水面上出现斜痕（slanting mark），则暗示有一个陡峭的暗礁（bluffreef）。如果光滑的水面上出现线条和环纹（lines and circles），则说明有危险的浅滩。
answers: Every day along its 1,200 miles, the Mississippi river delivered its wonder without reserve. It was so absorbing, so unflagging, and so sparking. The sunset upon the surface of the river was so wonderful. But now, for me, all the grace, the beauty, and the poetry of the river could never be restored. If the sun brightened the river, it meant that there would be wind the next day. If there was a floating log, it meant that the river was rising. A slanting mark sparkling on the water was a bluff reef. If there were lines and circles in the slick water, that showed troublesome places were dangerously shoaling up.
